page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed to support memory-heavy workloads requiring limited computational parallelism. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 processor architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache, as well as hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA-NI. The server features an expansive 512 GB of RAM, delivering 32 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance does not include a GPU, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, or local ephemeral disk storage, requiring all persistent data to reside on networked Azure storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier compute capabilities alongside robust memory subsystem bandwidth. The system posted a PassMark CPU score of 21,418.74 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 9,926.0, reflecting stable CPU execution under mixed instruction sets. Memory testing confirms throughput rates of 838.79 GB/s for small cached reads, 96.24 GB/s for large uncached reads, and 55.35 GB/s for uncached sequential writes. In caching operations, the server delivers 15.75 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by multi-threaded compression performance reaching 75.51 GB/s in bzip3 decompression tests.

By coupling 512 GB of RAM with a restricted 16-vCPU topology, the E64-16s_v5 presents favorable cost efficiency for enterprise applications constrained by per-core software licensing models. The trade-off is the total absence of integrated local storage, which mandates dependency on network-attached storage performance. This hardware composition is primarily suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching solutions like Redis and Memcached, analytics systems with significant RAM footprints, and data processing tasks requiring massive working memory without excessive compute overhead.
description: The Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads that require constrained compute capacity. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, the system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) based on the x86_64 architecture, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction set extensions. Featuring 512 GB of system RAM, it maintains an extensive 32 GB of memory per vCPU ratio. The configuration omits integrated local storage and hardware GPUs, directing persistent I/O workloads to external networked storage volumes. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance, marked by 15.75 million Redis SET operations per second and uncached read bandwidth of 96.24 GB/s. This hardware profile provides optimal qualitative cost efficiency for per-core licensed database software, large-scale in-memory caching tiers, enterprise relational databases, and memory-heavy analytical processing.
